_README: Corrections to committed result JSONs. MEASURED DATA IS NEVER MUTATED.
A result file on disk stays exactly as the job wrote it; this sidecar records
which DERIVED fields in it are wrong, why, and what replaces them. Read any
corrections are applied in memory, so a table built from JSON gets the same
Only derived fields are correctable. A measured accuracy, loss or timing is
never touched: if one of those is wrong the run is wrong and the fix is to
re-run it, not to edit it here.
Each entry carries: files, pointer (slash path into the JSON), op, value,
reason, provenance, added. op is one of set / remove / annotate.

corrections.reason: exp29's ratio arms were measured at FIVE epochs of recovery; this control ran TWO. The field scored a 5-epoch arm against a 2-epoch control, which reports the pruning cost plus the difference between two fine-tuning schedules as if it were the pruning cost alone. On this recipe the dense arm alone moves 1.11pp between 2 and 5 epochs. Each seed carries its own wrong triple, being exp29's mean minus that seed's own control: s42 -2.269 / -2.831 / -4.411, s123 -2.117 / -2.679 / -4.259, s456 -2.055 / -2.617 / -4.197, against matched three-seed costs of -1.30 / -1.93 / -3.91. No pruning cost is reportable from this pairing at all, so the field is removed rather than replaced.
corrections.provenance: experiments/exp31_dense_control.py now refuses this restatement unless args.epochs == EXP29_RATIO_EPOCHS; the fix landed after these three jobs ran, so the guard has never executed on real data. Correct 2-epoch costs: results/lumi_v060/EXP32_RATIO_AT_2EP.md, from exp32_ratios_s{42,123,456}/exp29_recovery.json.

corrections.reason: The file predates the epochs_matched field, so nothing in it tells a reader that the arm and the control were trained for different lengths. Without the flag the restated column looks like every other pruning cost in the corpus.
corrections.provenance: args.epochs == 2 in the same file; EXP29_RATIO_EPOCHS == 5 in experiments/exp31_dense_control.py.

corrections.value: WITHDRAWN restatement. exp29's ratio means are three-seed at FIVE epochs of recovery; this control ran TWO, so no pruning cost is derivable from the pairing and vs_this_control_pp has been removed. The claim 'this control is one seed' in the original note is also stale: exp32 ran three control seeds (81.676 / 81.524 / 81.462, mean 81.554). For the matched 2-epoch costs see results/lumi_v060/EXP32_RATIO_AT_2EP.md and results/lumi_v060/CONTROL_CONVENTION.md.
corrections.reason: The note was wrong in two independent ways: it presented the restatement as usable, and it described a three-seed control as single-seed.

The convention reports the fine-tuning gain separately from any pruning cost. The file has vs_pretrained_pp, which is the same quantity under a name that invites it to be read as a pruning result; the labelled field is added alongside without removing the original.
corrections.provenance: results/lumi_v060/CONTROL_CONVENTION.md. experiments/exp31_dense_control.py emits both names for runs after the fix.

value.caveat: The epoch counts match, so vs_this_control_pp IS a pruning cost here (-1.149 / -1.711 / -3.291). It is scored against a ONE-seed control (80.556%), where the write-ups use exp25's three-seed 80.44% and so report -1.03 / -1.59 / -3.17. Prefer the three-seed control; the 0.12pp difference between the two is control noise, not an effect.

corrections.reason: This restatement is correctly epoch-matched and must not be swept up with the exp32 one, but its control is single-seed and the published tables use a different, better control for the same cells. Without the annotation a reader cannot tell which of the two cost triples they are looking at.
corrections.provenance: results/lumi_v060/EXP25_ALIGNED.md for the three-seed control; results/lumi_v060/EXP29_RECOVERY_EPOCHS.md L206 already notes the single-seed path.
